title: Coach-plan workout detail (GET workout-service/fbt-adaptive/<workoutUuid>)
description:
Not wrapped by garminconnect — called directly via garmin.connectapi(f"workout-service/fbt-adaptive/{uuid}") (same connectapi-direct pattern as fitness_age.schema.json; drop the /gc-api gateway prefix the Garmin Connect page itself uses). workoutUuid comes from get_adaptive_training_plan_by_id's taskList[].taskWorkout.workoutUuid. Same overall shape as create_workout's own upload/get_workout_by_id response (workout_upload.schema.json) but this is the coach's real prescribed target detail — the source sync_training_plan's flat workoutDescription string (e.g. "137bpm") summarizes, but doesn't replace: 137 is the midpoint of a 124-149bpm range, not a hard cap (#97).

Verified against 3 real tasks, 2026-08-09: a single-step HR-zone run (Long Run, 124-149bpm), a 3-step pace-zone tempo run (Threshold: warmup/interval/cooldown, each with its own pace range — the interval step's range is the one that matters, not warmup/cooldown), and a strength RepeatGroupDTO (Total Body Circuit, no.target throughout, category/exerciseName same shape as create_workout's own steps). No rest-day sample captured — sync_training_plan does not currently fetch this endpoint for rest-day tasks (skipped entirely, since a rest day has no target to enrich), so that gap is intentionally out of scope rather than guessed at.

description.description: Same flat summary as taskWorkout.workoutDescription elsewhere (e.g. "137bpm") — not consumed here, sync_training_plan already has this from get_adaptive_training_plan_by_id directly.

workoutUuid.description: Matches the workoutUuid used to fetch this endpoint.

workoutSegments.description: One segment observed in every captured sample.

workoutSteps.description: ExecutableStepDTO entries directly, or one RepeatGroupDTO wrapping them (strength workouts) — same two shapes as workout_upload.schema.json's executableStep/repeatGroup. sync_training_plan picks the first ExecutableStepDTO step of stepType interval with a non-"no.target" targetType as "the" workout target (falling back to the first step with any real target at all) — a multi-step workout's warmup/cooldown legitimately carry a different, wider pace/HR range than its main interval, and the interval is what the coach's flat description string actually refers to.

workoutTargetTypeKey.description: no.target on strength steps and null-targetType steps; heart.rate.zone (id 4) or pace.zone (id 6, not previously seen elsewhere in this codebase) on running steps.

targetValueOne.description: Meaning depends on targetType: bpm (upper... actually lower, see targetValueTwo) bound for heart.rate.zone (observed 124 for a 124-149bpm range — targetValueOne is the LOW bound), m/s pace bound for pace.zone (observed 2.972 warmup / 3.555 interval — targetValueOne is the FASTER, i.e. numerically higher, m/s bound, which is the low end of the pace-per-km range), null for no.target/null targetType.

targetValueTwo.description: Paired with targetValueOne: bpm HIGH bound for heart.rate.zone (149 in the captured sample), the SLOWER (numerically lower) m/s bound for pace.zone (2.638 warmup / 3.277 interval), null otherwise.

category.description: Exercise catalog category on strength steps (e.g. "TOTAL_BODY"), null otherwise — same convention as workout_upload.schema.json.

workoutSteps.description: RepeatGroupDTO's children — same ExecutableStepDTO shape as this array's own items, one level deeper.
